findings.reason: The protected source is a concise sparse union-find solution with iterative path compression and union by size. It handles duplicate additions defensively, checks only four neighbors, decrements the count only for distinct-root unions, and uses names tied to genuine grid and disjoint-set concepts, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 305 and its Python numIslands2 surface plus app-local batch contract. The Reference preserves the initially-water grid model, four-directional connectivity, ordered additions and results, both source examples in order, five constraints, the follow-up, and an accessible text rendering of the source grid sequence.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064363029. It shares the exact helper and union-find data flow with the app-local source; the only executable surface difference is the permitted Solution.numIslands2 wrapper versus solve.

The legal 32, 128, and 256-addition chain tiers span 8x in k and exercise incremental connectivity while remaining within the grid-product and operation limits. The current source passes all nine selected executions with -0.00 relative growth and a 1.01x largest ratio; a correct implementation that recounts components after every addition passes every output but fails scaling at +1.03 and 32.24x.

The Approach now gives the row-times-width encoding its uniqueness justification and defines k before stating the near-linear union-find bounds. Its singleton, successful-union, duplicate, repeated-neighbor, and multi-bridge reasoning matches the protected implementation exactly.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against authenticated source evidence, including the two examples, the first example's full state progression, all five constraints, the follow-up, and the informational equivalent of the source image.

coverage: Both authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact dimensions, additions, and island-count sequences.
The invented duplicate-and-bridge row is now a trial rather than a source sample, and the formerly hidden bridge-plus-duplicate case is visible.
The one-cell source example covers all minimum input dimensions, while sparse one-row and one-column trials exercise the legal width and height maximum of 10,000 and both endpoint coordinates.
Duplicate-only, diagonal-only, out-of-order chain, and border additions verify idempotence, four-directional connectivity, and incremental component creation.

Two-component and four-component bridges verify one decrement per distinct-root union; a center touching four neighbors already in one component verifies that redundant same-root adjacencies do not over-decrement.

An independent flood-fill recount oracle verified all 13 authored results and all three benchmark results; the protected source also matched it on 87,308 exhaustive operation sequences of lengths one through five over every grid up to 3 by 3, including repeated coordinates.
All 13 correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 32-, 128-, and 256-addition scaling chains remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
